cards.a: A WAN that connects enterprise sites over a provider's L3VPN using PE routers that carry customer routes; the customer gets a private, any-to-any VPN while the SP handles routing between sites.

cards.q: What are the three device roles in an MPLS L3VPN model?
cards.a: CE (customer, connects to PE), PE (SP edge, runs VRF + MP-BGP), and P (SP core, forwards on labels).

cards.q: Which routing protocols can be used on the CE-PE link?
cards.a: eBGP (most common), OSPF (mutual redistribution), EIGRP (legacy), or static (simplest); the choice shapes the L3VPN design.

cards.q: What is the key contrast between MPLS L3VPN and Metro Ethernet?
cards.a: MPLS L3VPN is L3 with the provider doing routing and redundancy, while Metro Ethernet is L2 keeping routing and redundancy with the customer (any-to-any via VPLS/EVPN).

cards.q: What benefits does an MPLS L3VPN provide an enterprise?
cards.a: Private VRF isolation, any-to-any full mesh at no extra cost, managed routing by the SP, and provider-guaranteed SLA.

cards.q: How does dual-homing provide resilience in an MPLS WAN?
cards.a: Using dual PE and dual CE gives fast failover through routing, with BGP handling the path selection.

cards.q: Why is Internet traffic often kept off the MPLS private VPN?
cards.a: Internet often goes direct via DIA (direct Internet access), keeping MPLS reserved for private traffic; QoS is applied per-class over the VPN.

cards.q: Which commands verify an MPLS L3VPN?
cards.a: show ip route vrf CUST1 and ping vrf CUST1 verify routing; show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf CUST1 and show ip bgp vpnv4 all check MP-BGP; show mpls forwarding-table checks labels.

cards.q: No VPN routes are being received across an MPLS WAN. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An MP-BGP problem is likely; check show bgp vpnv4.

cards.q: A CE site is unreachable through the MPLS VPN. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A CE-PE protocol problem is likely; check show ip route vrf.

cards.q: MPLS forwarding is missing (no labels). What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An LDP/label problem is likely; check show mpls forwarding-table.

cards.q: VPN route overlap occurs between customers. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An RD (route distinguisher) overlap is likely; check the rd configuration.

cards.q: Summarize the MPLS WAN model and who routes.
cards.a: MPLS WAN is an SP-provided L3VPN using VRF + MP-BGP at the PE; the SP routes between sites (L3 = SP routes), while L2 Metro Ethernet keeps routing with the customer.
